quotes.text: This house was begun in 1839 for George Jones of Savannah. It was acquired in 1863 "by William King who named it Kings-cote, and the house remains in the King family. The orig-inal Gothic revival house was designed by Richard Upjohn, and the dining room addition of l880-l88l, one of the finest rooms of the period, was designed by Stanford White.
quotes.page: HABS No. RI-307, cover sheet; no numbered page marker was legible in this extract span

quotes.text: 1. Architectural character: A key example of Gothic Revival domestic architecture in America, the house is an important work of Richard Upjohn. The dining room addition of l880-l88l by Stanford White Is one of the finest interiors done in his early style.
quotes.page: HABS No. RI-307, Part II.A.1; no numbered page marker was legible in this extract span

quotes.text: 1. Over-all dimensions: Large irregular plan; original house one-and-a-half and two-and-a-half stories: 1880-1881 addition two-and-a-half and three stories.
quotes.page: HABS No. RI-307, Part II.B; the nearest page marker printed in the extract reads '"KIHGSCOTE" {George Jcnes-William H. King House) HAES No. RI-3C^ (Page-7)'

quotes.text: 2. Foundations: There are large cut granite blocks at the south and east sides. Random ashlar walls at the north and west show on the outside. Stone foundations show in the cellar except for poured concrete foundations in the new laundry wing at the rear.
quotes.page: HABS No. RI-307, Part II.B; the nearest page marker printed in the extract reads '"KIHGSCOTE" {George Jcnes-William H. King House) HAES No. RI-3C^ (Page-7)'

quotes.text: 3- Wall construction: The frame wall construction is covered by five inch wide ship-lap matched siding. Dining room addition has matched siding, five to eight inch widths on lower story and wooden shingles above. The house is painted grey with mold-ings picked out in red and black, probably the original color scheme.
quotes.page: HABS No. RI-307, Part II.B; the nearest page marker printed in the extract reads '"KIHGSCOTE" {George Jcnes-William H. King House) HAES No. RI-3C^ (Page-7)'

quotes.text: h. Structural system, framing: The heavy timber frame is mortised and tenoned.
quotes.page: HABS No. RI-307, Part II.B; the nearest page marker printed in the extract reads '"KIHGSCOTE" {George Jcnes-William H. King House) HAES No. RI-3C^ (Page-7)'

quotes.text: 5. Chimneys: There are four plastered brick chimneys with separate stacks on the original portion of the house. Two tall brick chimneys top the addition of l880-l88l.
quotes.page: HABS No. RI-307, Part II.B; the nearest page marker printed in the extract reads '"KIHGSCOTE" {George Jcnes-William H. King House) HAES No. RI-3C^ (Page-7)'

quotes.text: 6. Openings: a. Doorways: The main entrance on the south is centered in a wide entrance porch. The Tudor arched doorway has a two leaf door with tracery patterned paneling. b. Windows: Generally paired casement windows under label moldings, some with diamond patterned millions. There is colored glass in some windows, notably the Tiffany windows in the new dining room.
quotes.page: HABS No. RI-307, Part II.B; the nearest page marker printed in the extract reads '"KIHGSCOTE" {George Jcnes-William H. King House) HAES No. RI-3C^ (Page-7)'

quotes.text: 7- Roof: The steeply pitched roofs are intersected ~by numerous gables on the lower portions of the house. Higher roofs are hipped with lower pitches.
quotes.page: HABS No. RI-307, Part II.B; the nearest page marker printed in the extract reads '"KIHGSCOTE" {George Jcnes-William H. King House) HAES No. RI-3C^ (Page-7)'

quotes.text: The open eaves have elabo-rately sawn eave boards with pendants, barge boards, and shaped finials at the gable peaks.
quotes.page: HABS No. RI-307, Part II.B; the nearest page marker printed in the extract reads '"KIHGSCOTE" {George Jcnes-William H. King House) HAES No. RI-3C^ (Page-7)'

quotes.text: 8. Porches, stoops, and bulkheads: A one story porch on the east side opens to the double parlors through four French doors. The five wooden columns are quatrefoil in section. A cove roof with sawn pendant eaves and Gothic moldings decorates;-the porch. The entrance porch has three stone steps. The two service en-trance porches have three steps.
quotes.page: HABS No. RI-307, Part II.B; the nearest page marker printed in the extract reads '"KIHGSCOTE" {George Jcnes-William H. King House) HAES No. RI-3C^ (Page-7)'

quotes.text: C. Description of Interior: 1. Floor plan: The entrance hall is divided by a Gothic archway with two columns that separate the vestibule from the stairhall.
quotes.page: HABS No. RI-307 (Page 7); this span follows the page-7 running header directly in the extract
